summary: Umpqua NF lookout: camp 1912, cupola 1925, CCC L-4 cab 1933, R-6 cab 1958, removed 1977; four concrete footings reported in 2018, on a wilderness trail.

facts.design: R-6 flat cab (1958-1977); earlier D-6 cupola (1925) and L-4 cab (1933)
facts.status_note: Removed in 1977 per the registry and two other pages (firelookout.com says destroyed); four concrete footings reported in 2018

access.note: Reached by Forest Service Trail #1580 from Grasshopper Trail #1574 via Acker Divide Trailhead; inside Rogue-Umpqua Divide Wilderness, wilderness restrictions apply

visit.trail_note: Trail ends at the former lookout site with 800-foot cliffs and views of Cliff and Buckeye Lakes; no water available on the trail; snow cover mid-fall to mid-spring

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Umpqua National Forest

events.note: Camp set up at the site before any cupola cabin
Victor Boyd left for Tiller to be stationed at the Grasshopper ranger lookout
Lookout-fireman Walter Lerwell reported the first fire at 4 p.m. and had it under control before night (Roseburg News-Review, as quoted on Forest Lookouts)
L-4 cab on a round timber tower about 10 ft tall, built by the CCC; the new lookout was meant to replace the old one
Prefabricated R-6 flat cab replaced the L-4 cab; about 3,800 lb of materials flown in by helicopter
Euberto Newton of Tiller lived in a tent about a month while the old house was torn down
Roger E. Lamb, a college student, stationed at Grasshopper Mountain for the summer
Removed per the registry, Forest Lookouts and the 2018 blog; firelookout.com says destroyed
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on December 19, 2010
Hike report counts four concrete footings remaining at the top

corrections.proposed: R-6 flat cab (1958-1977); earlier D-6 cupola (1925) and L-4 cab (1933)
corrections.why: The brief names only the 1925 D-6 cupola. Sources say the cab standing until 1977 was an R-6 flat cab installed in 1958.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The registry, Forest Lookouts and the 2018 hike report say removed in 1977; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1977. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Brief design D-6 covers only the 1925 cupola; corrected in corrections. Height 3.0 m is the 10 ft tower. The FFLOS register lists the date registered as December 19, 2010, so a 2010 registration event is included. A second Forest Lookouts page (grasshopper-mountain.html, 1938 and 1941 staffing) appeared only in search snippets and was not read, so it is not used. Access is public per the Forest Service trail page, which notes wilderness rules. No photos with stable image URLs were found.
